Roti Cenai

Sheldo’s kitchen102 hours2 hours4 hours

Flaky flatbreads only found in Malaysian fast food stalls. Best eaten with a curry dip.

  • Dough:
  • 300 mL lukewarm water + up to 15 mL more if needed
  • 60 g sweetened condensed milk
  • 35 g melted butter or ghee
  • 12 g fine sea salt or table salt
  • 20 g sugar
  • 600 g all-purpose flour
  • Shaping:
  • 120 mL neutral oil approximate for coating
  • Cooking:
  • Ghee or neutral oil + butter amount as needed
  • Dairy-Free Dough Option:
  • 300 mL oat, almond, soy, or lactose-free milk
  • 35 g melted margarine or vegan butter
  • 12 g fine sea salt or table salt
  • 54 g sugar
  • 600 g all-purpose flour
  • Super Coconut-y Curry Dip:
  • 240 mL full-fat coconut milk 120 mL + 120 mL
  • 40–45 g Thai red curry paste
  • 0.5 g turmeric
  • 1 g five spice or garam masala
  • 60 mL water
  • 3–5 mL fish sauce or substitute with soy sauce
  • 1 g sugar
  • Salt to taste

Make Dough:

  1. In a large mixing bowl, combine water, condensed milk, melted butter or ghee, salt, and sugar. Stir until fully dissolved.
  2. Add flour and stir with a spatula. Switch to hands and knead until dough comes together. Add up to 15 mL extra water if needed to incorporate all flour. Stop kneading once smooth and free of dry bits; dough will still look rough.
  3. Cover and let rest for 15 minutes.
  4. Knead again briefly (about 30 seconds) until smooth.
  5. Divide into 10 equal balls, ~100 g each. Shape tightly and smoothly.
  6. Add ~80 mL oil to a tray and spread evenly. Coat each dough ball in oil generously.
  7. Cover tray tightly. Rest at room temperature for 1–3 hours, or refrigerate overnight for best results. Let come to room temp 1 hour before use if chilled.

Stretch & Shape:

  1. Stretch each ball into a large, thin sheet by tossing/stretching or rolling/stretching. Fold top/bottom to center, then left/right. Add a bit more oil and let rest while shaping the rest.

Cook:

  1. Preheat a non-stick skillet over medium heat (about 2–3 minutes).
  2. Re-stretch shaped roti just before cooking.
  3. Add 30–45 mL ghee or oil to the pan. When shimmering, add roti. Cook until bottom is golden. If it puffs, press gently to ensure even browning.
  4. Flip and cook the other side. If using ghee, cook until both sides are golden. If using oil, once second side is lightly golden, add 15–30 g butter, swirl to coat, and cook until golden.
  5. Transfer roti to a clean tea towel. Let rest for 30 seconds, then clap between hands (protected by towel) to fluff and separate layers. Serve immediately with curry dip.

Coconut Curry Dip:

  1. Add 120 mL coconut milk to a small pot. Heat over medium and reduce until thick and oil starts separating (about 5 minutes).Stir in curry paste and fry until red oil appears. Add turmeric and five spice, stir and cook 20 seconds.
  2. Add remaining 120 mL coconut milk, 60 mL water, and fish/soy sauce. Simmer 5 minutes.
  3. Add sugar and salt to taste. Adjust the consistency with water; it should resemble heavy cream with a red oil layer on top.
  4. Serve warm with fresh roti. Reheat if solidified.
